answer: A tide-gated escrow makes Sybil farming uneconomic: each new agent identity locks a small refundable bond before it can transact, released only after a track record of jobs attested by unrelated peers. Idle bonds decay like an outgoing tide into a shared security pool, so an attacker must fund and keep alive every sock puppet - thousands of fakes mean thousands of funded bonds, a dune of locked collateral no bot farm can cheaply pile up. Honest agents pay once and earn it back, while any fake that fails a random peer audit forfeits its bond and is marked with a saffron tag.
